# CLI reference

## help

Print the verb list as JSON (for SessionStart and SessionEnd reason=compact hooks). CLI aliases: --help, -h.

### Parameters

_None._

### Result

- `verbs` ([]VerbSummary): Array of {name, description} for every verb in the manifest.

### Errors

_None._

## spawn

Launch a tracked agent in a new tmux session. Returns the instance_id and pre_trust (ok, skipped or failed) without waiting for the agent; the row is pending from its insert until the agent reports in, then waiting. Creating its labelled session is bounded by the create timeout; on a timeout it returns ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE, transient): the session may have been created and the new row stays pending; do not retry until get shows the row ended or missing, since a retry without an explicit id would start a second agent; then retry an explicit id with the reuse opt-in and the row's agent, which get shows. A session of this store labelled with an explicit id that has no row, left over from an earlier life, refuses the spawn with ErrTmuxSessionConflict; nothing is written. If the session name is already held, spawn ends its new row at once (unless the error says otherwise) and returns ErrTmuxSessionConflict naming the holder's tmux id and whether its label names this id; ErrTmuxSessionCreate (LAUNCH FAILURE) if the holder vanished first, ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT) or ErrTmuxUnresponsive if tmux could not be run or read. ErrTmuxSessionConflict is CONFLICT (permanent until a human looks): another row's or another agent-director store's session is another agent and must not be ended; a leftover of an earlier life or a session with no valid instance id is a human's to end (see docs/operator-actions.md); then, if refused for a held name, spawn the id again with reuse_finished (--reuse-finished on the CLI) and the row's agent. ErrInternal, nothing created or changed: the collision pre-check could not read the store (which says nothing about whether the id is in use), or a reuse's archive of the previous session or its change failed (a busy store included), or a reused row's recorded name is unusable (see kill). To end a live row (pending included) and relaunch its id, follow the live-row sequence in kill's description.

### Parameters

- `cwd` (string, required): Absolute (or ~/-prefixed) path the Spawn's agent starts in. Required.
- `template` (string, optional): Optional named template under ~/.config/agent-director/templates/. Per-call params layer on top (scalars replace; maps merge; permissions arrays concat; agent_args replaces wholesale).
- `agent` (string, optional): The agent to launch: claude (Claude Code) or codex (Codex), case-sensitive; empty or absent means not given. A per-call agent overrides the template's; with neither, ErrAgentMissing; any other value, ErrAgentInvalid. A template's non-empty agent_args are inherited only when the template's agent is this agent, else ErrAgentArgsMismatch (this call's own non-empty agent_args replace them). A codex spawn with any allow, deny or ask entry, from the call or the template, is refused with ErrPermissionsUnsupported. The row records the agent for life; get and list show it.
- `instance_id` (string, optional): Optional explicit id; an empty or absent id mints a fresh UUID4. An explicit id containing an ASCII control character (0x00-0x1f or 0x7f) is rejected with ErrInvalidFlags. An explicit id that already has a row returns ErrInstanceIdCollision: without the reuse opt-in any existing row collides, in any state; with it, only a live row (pending included) or a row that changed or was removed after this spawn examined it.
- `label` ([]string, optional): Label k=v entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag). Each becomes AGENT_DIRECTOR_LABEL_<UPPER_KEY> on the session env and persists in labels.
- `allow` ([]string, optional): permissions.allow entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `deny` ([]string, optional): permissions.deny entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `ask` ([]string, optional): permissions.ask entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `relay_mode` (string, optional): on / off. Empty falls back to config defaults.relay_mode (default off). Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) knows this parameter only as relay-mode and silently ignores relay_mode.
- `extra_env` (map[string]string, optional): Env-var entries injected on the tmux session env, as an object mapping each variable name to its value (on the CLI, a repeatable KEY=VALUE flag). Keys rejected with ErrReservedEnvKey, a template's included, never rewritten: the reserved names AGENT_DIRECTOR_* and HOME with any value (an extra_env HOME would move the agent's hook to another agent-director store; set an absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code) or CODEX_HOME (Codex) to give the agent its own config), and a key that is not a valid env-var name (empty, or containing '=' or a NUL byte, which tmux would read as a different variable; the message says which); auth env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) allowed. Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) knows this parameter only as extra-env and silently ignores extra_env, so its variables (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME included) are not set.
- `agent_args` ([]string, optional): Pass-through argv to the agent program, one argument per array element (on the CLI, the arguments after --). Claude refuses --settings, --output-format and print (-p/--print, clusters included). Session selectors/owned values are refused except on a finished-agent switch: dropped_args reports their removal; the agent starts fresh and resumes nothing. Exact denied long tokens owned as values always refuse. For a codex agent, refused (ErrSpawnDeniedFlag): a Codex subcommand in command position, --remote, --remote-auth-token-env, -c/--config keys at, above or under hooks, tui.disable_paste_burst or features.hooks, and --disable hooks; with disable_ask_user on, also --enable default_mode_request_user_input and the question-tool keys. agent-director adds no second --no-daemon, --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (pre-trust ok) or --enable write_stdin_approval when the arguments already carry one before any --; Codex rejects a flag the arguments themselves repeat.
- `no_pre_trust` (bool, optional): Skip the folder pre-trust. For a claude agent, pre-trust pre-writes projects.<cwd>.hasTrustDialogAccepted=true into the spawn's .claude.json (resolves to <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json if CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set in extra_env, otherwise ~/.claude.json). For a codex agent, it puts the cwd's trust and the hook-trust bypass on the launch's command line and writes no file, so Codex does not stop at its folder-trust prompt. Default off (pre-trust IS performed so the agent skips its workspace-trust dialog and the Spawn becomes interactive immediately). The choice is recorded on the row until the next spawn or reuse, and every resume follows it: no pre-trust is attempted over an opt-out. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling.
- `tmux_session_name` (string, optional): Optional explicit tmux session name. Empty/omitted falls back to <basename(cwd)>-<id[:8]>. Validated app-side: rejects empty (when supplied), '#' ':' '.' '$' '\' (backslash), ASCII control chars, non-UTF-8, and >64 bytes. NO DB uniqueness check; a name already held by a tmux session when spawn creates its session ends the new row at once and returns the classified error spawn's description states (ErrTmuxSessionConflict naming the holding session), unless spawn refused earlier and wrote nothing. Name reuse across ended spawns is supported. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling.
- `reuse_finished` (bool, optional): Opt in to reusing an explicit instance_id whose row is finished (ended or missing): the id starts again on that row. A live row (pending included) still collides with ErrInstanceIdCollision, as does a row that changed or was removed after this spawn examined it; nothing is changed then. No effect without an explicit instance_id (a minted id cannot collide). Applies to this call only; no template or config setting carries it. The default (off) is unchanged: any existing row with the id collides. With no dropped arguments, a successful spawn does not say whether it created a fresh row or reset a finished one. Nonempty dropped_args identifies reuse that switches a finished row's agent; the CLI prints a notice when arguments are dropped. The spawn names its agent (agent, or the template's) and the reused row takes it: to reuse a row for the agent it ran, pass the row's agent, which get shows. Only an agent switch starts a new life; same-agent reuse keeps session history and subagent records but starts a fresh conversation. A switch back also starts with no memory of its earlier lives: resume and get never use or show an earlier life's history. Resume continues only the latest session; older sessions remain listed for inspection only. Retrying a failed plain spawn: after a held-name refusal (duplicate session) the row is already ended unless the error says otherwise, so the retry's lookup decides it at once; after any other failed launch the row stays pending and an opted-in retry collides until find-missing marks it missing, which happens only after the pending grace period (60 s by default). Feature detection: read the version of the binary that serves the caller: on the CLI the version verb; over MCP the version tool, which reports the running serve process's version until that process restarts; in the TypeScript client binaryVersion (from Client.create() or resolveSystemBinary()), never version(), which is the npm package's version. A release candidate X.Y.Z-rc.N counts as X.Y.Z. A build without a release stamp reports 0.0.0-dev (a make build) or dev (a plain go build); a caller cannot compare it and relies on the older-binary behaviour: an older binary returns ErrInvalidFlags on the CLI and in the TypeScript client, and over MCP silently ignores the parameter, so a finished row gives ErrInstanceIdCollision. Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0 and knows this parameter only as reuse-finished) silently ignores reuse_finished, so a finished row gives ErrInstanceIdCollision. Use it as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents. So kill's success on a finished row is not verification of exit; on the wrong tmux server, a row wrongly marked missing, kill's no-op success and a reuse together start a second agent for the same id.

### Result

- `instance_id` (string): The id (caller-supplied or freshly-minted UUID4) the row is tracked under.
- `pre_trust` (string): What the launch's folder-trust pre-trust did. ok = the folder trust took effect (claude: the entry was written to .claude.json; codex: the launch carries the folder trust and the hook-trust bypass); skipped = pre-trust was off for this launch because the caller passed no_pre_trust, so nothing was attempted; failed = pre-trust was attempted and the entry was not written (for a claude agent, the .claude.json file is missing, or could not be read, parsed or written, or extra_env sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a path that is not absolute; for a codex agent, extra_env sets CODEX_HOME to a path that is not absolute, and the launch carries neither the folder trust nor the hook-trust bypass); the launch still proceeds and the agent may stop at its folder-trust prompt (Claude Code's or Codex's).
- `dropped_args` ([]string): Original resume arguments removed on a finished-agent switch, in argv order. Omitted when empty; starts fresh and resumes nothing.

## status

Return a row's state (pending/waiting/working/ask_user/check_permission/ended/missing). pending means a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) is in progress and the agent has not reported in yet (its SessionStart hook); it may be loading or at a startup prompt. A resumed pending row keeps its session id and history.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to inspect.

### Result

- `state` (string): Current state, one of the allowed values. pending: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) is in progress and the agent has not reported in yet (its SessionStart hook); it may be loading or waiting at a startup prompt. A resumed pending row keeps its session id and history (non-empty session_id). `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. With [state] settle_ms set in config.toml (whole milliseconds from 0 to 60000, 0 or unset is off; a value outside that range is refused, never capped), state is the settled state: a state a hook wrote shows only once it has held that long, and the last settled state shows meanwhile, so a change that reverts sooner never shows; ended, missing and a state a command wrote (spawn, resume, find-missing) show at once. Nothing marks a state as late, and the setting covers every caller on the host. A turn shorter than settle_ms never shows (a waiting agent that replies sooner reads waiting throughout), so keep it at 1000 to 2000. The row's other fields, and the verbs that act on it (send-keys, decide, pause, resume, kill, find-missing, expire, spawn), follow its live state, which can be newer: a refusal can name a state status does not show yet.
- `launch_started_at` (timestamp?): Start of the launch in progress: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision. Present only while the row is pending; omitted otherwise. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms.

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

## get

Return a row in full (id, parent, state, cwd, session name, tmux socket, args, relay mode, session_id, labels, timestamps).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to fetch.

### Result

- `instance_id` (string): Stable id of the Spawn.
- `parent_id` (string): Parent Spawn id (AGENT_DIRECTOR_INSTANCE_ID env at spawn time), empty when launched by a human shell.
- `state` (string): Current state, one of the allowed values. pending: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) is in progress and the agent has not reported in yet (its SessionStart hook); it may be loading or waiting at a startup prompt. A resumed pending row keeps its session id and history (non-empty session_id). `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. With [state] settle_ms set in config.toml (whole milliseconds from 0 to 60000, 0 or unset is off; a value outside that range is refused, never capped), state is the settled state: a state a hook wrote shows only once it has held that long, and the last settled state shows meanwhile, so a change that reverts sooner never shows; ended, missing and a state a command wrote (spawn, resume, find-missing) show at once. Nothing marks a state as late, and the setting covers every caller on the host. A turn shorter than settle_ms never shows (a waiting agent that replies sooner reads waiting throughout), so keep it at 1000 to 2000. The row's other fields, and the verbs that act on it (send-keys, decide, pause, resume, kill, find-missing, expire, spawn), follow its live state, which can be newer: a refusal can name a state status does not show yet.
- `cwd` (string): Canonicalized cwd.
- `agent` (string): The agent the row runs: claude (Claude Code) or codex (Codex). Set at spawn, replaced by a reuse, followed by resume.
- `tmux_session_name` (string): tmux session under which the Spawn is running.
- `tmux_socket` (string?): The tmux socket the row's launch uses; omitted when the row has no recorded socket.
- `agent_args` ([]string): Verbatim argv passed through to the agent program.
- `relay_mode` (string): on / off.
- `jsonl_path` (string): Current session's transcript path, persisted by the hooks; legacy rows may be empty. Resume tries this path, then for claude recomputes the current session's path from cwd + session_id (under a usable absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from extra_env, otherwise ~/.claude). A codex row uses only its recorded path; resume never builds one for it. Older sessions are never candidates.
- `session_id` (string): Agent session id, recorded from the agent's hooks: Claude's is its transcript file's name, Codex's the session_id its hooks report. Empty until the first SessionStart.
- `labels` (map[string]string): Caller-supplied labels.
- `started_at` (timestamp): Row insert time.
- `last_seen_at` (timestamp): Last hook UPSERT time.
- `ended_at` (timestamp?): Set when state moves to ended (omitted while live).
- `launch_started_at` (timestamp?): Start of the launch in progress: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision. Present only while the row is pending; omitted otherwise. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms.
- `liveness_unverified_since` (timestamp?): RFC3339 timestamp of the first sweep that noted this live row (left it unverified, or noted it unreported); kept while later sweeps change liveness_note, unreported included. Cleared to NULL together with liveness_note when a sweep finds the agent process alive, except on a pending row it notes unreported and a pending row noted provenance_conflict, which keeps it; null/omitted while the row has no note.
- `liveness_note` (string?): Reason token of the latest sweep that left this live row unverified (its agent process could not be checked and tmux did not settle it), for example process_not_seen_session_present, process_not_seen_tmux_unchecked, probe_eacces, tmux_server_changed or provenance_conflict; overwritten when the reason changes. Cleared to NULL together with liveness_unverified_since when a sweep finds the agent process alive, except on a pending row it notes unreported and a pending row noted provenance_conflict, which keeps it; null/omitted while the row has no note. Or unreported, on a pending row past the pending grace period: its agent is alive, but no hook has reported since its launch, so it may sit at an agent startup screen or idle at its prompt. The row stays pending. To act on it: read-pane, then send-keys with allow_pending (--allow-pending on the CLI); only a caller that looked should type. A later sweep that finds the agent alive keeps the note; the agent's next hook clears it. unreported never replaces provenance_conflict.
- `permission_requests` ([]object): Open permission requests: those that still await an answer (not acked by their relay hook and not answered at the pane, decided or not; a request with no recorded settle instant while undecided). Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Populated only when the row's live state is check_permission; empty array for all other states (a row can read waiting, working or ask_user while a request is still open: follow a tracked request with get-permission). Requests are never delayed by [state] settle_ms, so with it set a row can also read any state (even ended or missing) with open requests listed, or check_permission with [], for up to settle_ms. Each element: request_id (int) — autoincrement row id; request_token (string) — UUIDv4 request token, pass to decide verb to target this row; tool_name (string) — the agent's tool that triggered the request; tool_input (string) — raw JSON string of the tool's input, NOT a nested object (consumers parse it themselves); requested_at (RFC3339 timestamp) — when the request was recorded; decision and decision_reason (string?) — the recorded verdict, not the outcome; and the delivery facts as get-permission returns them: delivery (delivered, not_confirmed or fallen_back), confirm_by (timestamp), hook_alive (bool?), hook_gone_at (timestamp?), attempted_decision (string?), attempted_at (timestamp?), tool_use_id (string?), pane_answer (none or intent on an open request), pane_as (string?), proven_gone_at (timestamp?), proven_gone_how (string?) and unproven_since (timestamp?). get and list never wait for the store's write lock.
- `unproven_requests` ([]object): Every permission request of the row that the agent has not proven gone (proven_gone_at null), oldest first, in any state but ended and missing ([] on those). Unlike permission_requests it also lists requests agent-director's records read closed (delivered, answered at the pane, or recorded answered outside it), each with unproven_since: a request that stays unproven a while after it is a reason to read the pane, since its dialog may still be on it. Elements have the same fields as permission_requests'. While it is not empty, plain send-keys without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused. Always a non-null array. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row can read ended or missing with requests here for up to settle_ms.
- `transcript_status` (string): Derived operator-facing summary of the current session's transcript state: 'present' (jsonl_path recorded), 'never_written' (session id but NULL jsonl_path and prior_sessions is empty — nothing was ever written in the current life), 'rotated' (NULL jsonl_path but prior_sessions is non-empty — the current life has history under a different session id), or 'no_session' (no session_id yet). Session history belongs to a life; 'never_written' and 'rotated' are decided on the same entries prior_sessions lists. Same-agent reuse retains the history; an agent switch or switch back starts a new life with no history. A failed reuse's applied restore returns the pre-reuse life.
- `prior_sessions` ([]object): Archived prior sessions of the current life, newest first, excluding the row's current session id. Same-agent reuse retains session history; an agent switch or switch back starts a new life, hiding earlier lives. Resume continues only the current session; older sessions are listed for inspection only. A failed reuse's applied restore returns the pre-reuse life's history. Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Each element: session_id (string) — archived session id; jsonl_path (string) — archived transcript path (may be empty); recorded_at (timestamp) — when the archive was written (the rotation moment).

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

## send-keys

Ordinary: readiness, 512-byte UTF-8 chunks/drain, one Enter, exact transcript proof. ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed: not_started/partial_input_unconfirmed/submission_unconfirmed; no replay. key/no_enter/empty text/pane hashes: manual. ErrTmuxSendKeys (GONE: the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the live Spawn to drive.
- `text` (string, optional): Text to type into the Spawn's input. `\r` stripped pre-send; `\n` preserved as newline-in-input. Empty/omitted: nothing typed (Enter only, unless no_enter or key). Exclusive with key; must be empty on a pane answer.
- `delivery_request_id` (string, optional): Owns one ordinary text attempt on this launch (1-128 letters, digits, underscore or hyphen). Retry the same id and normalized text to observe without replay. A fresh id permits an intentional identical turn. Omitted ids conservatively reuse the last confirmed identical payload. Unresolved input blocks new automatic writes. Exclusive with manual key, no_enter, pane hash and permission answers.
- `allow_pending` (bool, optional): When true, also allows a pending row: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) whose agent has not reported in yet. Keys are delivered only to a session started by the row's current launch. ended and missing rows are still rejected for new input (ErrSpawnNotInteractive); an existing ordinary request can return stored or late proof without input.
- `no_enter` (bool, optional): Type text with no Enter after it. With neither text nor key: ErrInvalidFlags (nothing to send). A pane answer never presses Enter.
- `key` (string, optional): Send this one key instead of text, never followed by Enter: a named key (Escape, Enter, Up, Down, Tab), sent by name, or one character, typed literally. The caller picks the key; agent-director never interprets the screen. Required on a pane answer. Anything else: ErrInvalidFlags.
- `expect_pane_sha256` (string, optional): Required on a pane answer, optional otherwise. The pane_sha256 read-pane returned for the pane the caller looked at (64 hex digits). Before acting, the agent's pane is captured with the same n_lines, ANSI stripped as read-pane gives it by default, and its SHA-256 compared byte for byte; a difference is ErrPaneChanged, nothing done, and the error does not carry the new hash: read the pane again. It means a person or LLM judged this exact screen: never pass it from an automatic flow. On a plain call a matching hash also passes the hold of a request not proven gone (ErrDialogMaybeOpen); every other refusal still applies.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): The n_lines of the read-pane expect_pane_sha256 came from. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted.
- `request_token` (string, optional): Makes the call a pane answer to this permission request of the Spawn (as get, get-permission or ErrRelayFallenBack's err_details name it): with as, key and expect_pane_sha256, and no text, it sends exactly one key and never Enter. Accepted only once the request has fallen back (its relay hook gone, no verdict acked, no pane answer completed), while no relay hook of the Spawn may still answer (else ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed) and no other pane answer on it is still being sent (else ErrPaneAnswerInProgress). pane_answer intent means sending started but whether the key was sent is unknown; sent records the key was sent, with decision as and decision_reason pane. Not open: ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest or ErrAlreadyDecided. A retry after a sender that died is accepted with a fresh hash. Without it the call is plain: refused with ErrRelayFallenBack (with err_details) while any request of the Spawn has fallen back with no pane answer recorded, then, without expect_pane_sha256, with ErrDialogMaybeOpen (with err_details) while any request of the Spawn is not proven gone by the agent (get's unproven_requests), whatever agent-director's records say of it.
- `as` (string, optional): A pane answer's claimed verdict, allow or deny: recorded as the request's pane_as and, once its key is sent, its decision. The caller's claim: agent-director never checks it against the key. Only with request_token.

### Result

- `request_id` (string): Ordinary delivery attempt identity; absent on manual operations.
- `outcome` (string): submitted only with exact native transcript proof; absent on manual operations.
- `session_id` (string): Native session that recorded the ordinary prompt.
- `record_id` (string): Native user record id when provided by the pinned schema.
- `record_sha256` (string): SHA-256 of the exact structured user record.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`
- `ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed`
- `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrDialogMaybeOpen`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrPaneAnswerInProgress`
- `ErrPaneChanged`
- `ErrStoreBusy`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSendKeys`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## read-pane

Capture the last N lines of the agent's own pane (default 25, no upper cap). ANSI escapes stripped, unicode glyphs kept, unless `ansi=true` (raw bytes). tmux errors: ErrTmuxCaptureFailed (GONE: only it means the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to read.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): Number of trailing pane lines to return. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted. No upper cap. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `ansi` (bool, optional): When true, return raw bytes from tmux (escape codes preserved). When false (default), strip ANSI sequences while preserving unicode glyphs.
- `allow_pending` (bool, optional): No effect: pending, ended and missing rows are all readable.

### Result

- `pane` (string): Captured pane text. ANSI handling depends on the `ansi` parameter.
- `pane_sha256` (string): SHA-256, lowercase hex, of exactly the bytes of pane. Pass it as send-keys' or record-pane-answer's expect_pane_sha256, with the same n_lines, when acting on what this pane shows; they compare it with the pane captured as read-pane gives it by default (ANSI stripped), so the hash of an ansi=true read never matches. A checksum: agent-director does not look at what the bytes say.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## kill

End the agent of a live row's current launch (pending included). kill finds the session with that launch's label on the row's recorded socket, ends the agent's pane and that session by tmux id, and succeeds only once the agent process and every other process found in the session's panes are gone; otherwise it returns ErrTmuxKillFailed. kill_sent says whether a kill was sent. With no session of the launch found, an agent process gone or not recorded is success, nothing sent; one running in another session's pane has that pane ended and is checked again. On a finished row (ended or missing) kill is a no-op success with kill_sent false and no tmux call. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). kill never changes the row's state: find-missing marks it once its agent process is gone. kill never signals a process itself; one the agent started can outlive a successful kill. On a pending row, before the launch created its session, kill returns kill_sent false and does not stop the launch. kill never ends an earlier launch's session. Success is judged per call: if ErrTmuxKillFailed named a non-agent process outliving the kill, later calls do not track it: a retried kill checks only the agent process. A retry's success means only that the agent is gone; the named process needs a human (see docs/operator-actions.md). If the row finishes while kill waits and the agent outlives the wait, kill returns ErrTmuxKillFailed; a retried kill is a finished-row no-op. Errors (for kill, GONE is success): ErrTmuxKillFailed (UNAVAILABLE): after a kill the agent process or another process of the session's panes ran past the kill exit wait, or the process cannot be checked and its labelled session remains, or no session or pane of this launch was found while the agent process runs; retry later. ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE): tmux did not answer usably, before or after a kill was sent; retry later with backoff. ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT, permanent until a human looks): the session found is not this launch's, or tmux holds conflicting labels; no kill was sent (see docs/operator-actions.md). ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT): tmux could not be run, its socket is not accessible to this user, or this is not the agent's tmux server; an operator must fix it. A repeated kill right after the last session on its tmux server ends can get ErrTmuxUnresponsive or ErrTmuxNotAvailable while the server exits; the caller waits and checks again. ErrSpawnNotFound: no row has this id. None of these errors means that the agent is dead. kill must run as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents. So kill's success on a finished row is not verification of exit; on the wrong tmux server, a row wrongly marked missing, kill's no-op success and a reuse together start a second agent for the same id. Agents never run expire (operator-scheduled finished-row cleanup). A live row whose recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, or containing a control character or a character tmux stores differently) gets ErrInternal with no tmux call; removing the row is a human's decision (see docs/operator-actions.md). Live-row sequence (a pending row included): 1. kill and check the result; on an error follow its class. 2. If pending, wait until its launch start (status) plus the pending grace period (60 s unless configured); inside it, wait and check again, never escalate. 3. Run find-missing, then check status; repeat about 5 s apart until ended or missing, at most three runs. 4. Still live: kill once more, wait about 5 s, run find-missing once more and check. 5. Still live: escalate to a human. 6. Then resume the row if it has a session id and the caller wants the conversation back; otherwise spawn with reuse_finished (--reuse-finished on the CLI) and the row's agent, which get shows; callers whose ids agent-director mints spawn fresh.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to kill.

### Result

- `kill_sent` (bool): True exactly when a pane kill or a session kill was sent, including one whose call failed; false when no kill was sent, for example for a finished row.

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxKillFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## decide

Caller's allow/deny verdict on an open PermissionRequest (relay_mode=on only). Records it, first call wins (else ErrAlreadyDecided), waits up to 1 s for the relay hook's ack and returns delivery: delivered, or not_confirmed (poll get-permission; it ends by confirm_by). A request whose relay hook is gone is refused at once with ErrRelayFallenBack. ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest (none open by that token, spawn ended or missing, or dialog may have closed): do not answer at the pane. max_wait_ms prevents a required wait before recording: ErrStoreBusy.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn sitting on the PermissionRequest.
- `request_token` (string, required): UUIDv4 token identifying the specific permission request to decide. Required to select one request when the Spawn has several.
- `decision` (string, required): Either `allow` or `deny`.
- `reason` (string, optional): Accepted but ignored; a deny records decision_reason operator regardless of this value.
- `max_wait_ms` (int, optional): Optional bound on the whole call, in milliseconds from its start (no default). Required waits before recording, for the store or a request with no recorded settle instant, respect the bound; if they cannot finish in time, ErrStoreBusy records nothing and a retry is safe. With no time left, recording proceeds only if the store is free at once. The wait for the relay hook's ack also ends at the bound, with not_confirmed: once the verdict is recorded decide never returns ErrStoreBusy. A caller with a deadline passes at most its deadline minus 1 s. Omitted: no bound, the store's busy timeout applies. Negative: ErrInvalidFlags.

### Result

- `delivery` (string): delivered: the relay hook acknowledged the verdict. not_confirmed: no ack within decide's wait of at most 1 s (or by the max_wait_ms bound); ask get-permission, at the latest at confirm_by, by when it is delivered or fallen_back. decide never returns fallen_back: such a request is refused with ErrRelayFallenBack, or ErrAlreadyDecided once answered at the pane.
- `confirm_by` (timestamp): RFC3339 time by which not_confirmed ends: the relay hook's kill instant plus 2 s, by when its hook has acked (delivered) or is gone (fallen_back). With no recorded settle instant: requested_at plus the relay window plus 2 s.
- `hook_alive` (bool?): Whether the request's relay hook process runs, checked in the reader's pid namespace by its pid and start time: true; false (no such process, another start time, or a zombie); null when it cannot be checked (another or unreadable pid namespace, unreadable /proc, or no recorded hook identity).
- `hook_gone_at` (timestamp?): When a reader first found the request fallen back; null until then. A reading verb (get, list, get-permission) records it only if the store's write lock is free at that moment, never waiting.
- `attempted_decision` (string?): The verdict a decide refused as fallen back (ErrRelayFallenBack) tried to record, the latest one; null when none. Stored and shown, never acted on.
- `attempted_at` (timestamp?): When that refused decide ran; null when none.
- `tool_use_id` (string?): The permission request's tool_use_id from the agent's hook input; null when none was given.
- `pane_answer` (string): How the request was answered at the pane. none: no pane answer recorded through agent-director (something outside it, such as a person at tmux, may still have answered it). intent: a pane answer through send-keys was started and whether its key was typed is unknown. sent: its key was sent (decision_reason pane). outside: a caller recorded it answered outside agent-director (record-pane-answer, decision_reason pane_outside). tool_ran: the agent reported its tool ran (decision allow, decision_reason tool_ran). A request with sent, outside or tool_ran is closed and stays delivery fallen_back.
- `pane_as` (string?): The verdict a pane answer claims: allow, deny, or unknown (an outside record that did not see the answer); null when none was recorded. The caller's claim, stored and never checked.
- `proven_gone_at` (timestamp?): When the agent proved the request's permission dialog gone; null until then. agent-director's own records (delivered, a pane answer, record-pane-answer) are not proof. While it is null, plain send-keys to the live spawn without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused (ErrDialogMaybeOpen).
- `proven_gone_how` (string?): How it was proven gone. tool_ran: a Claude PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure carried its tool_use_id (never on a Codex row). turn_end: the turn of the agent that asked ended after it was written; the main agent's Stop or idle-prompt Notification, or a Codex main agent's Interrupt (Esc), proves a request with no agent_id (including a main-agent request). agent_gone: its spawn was marked missing, ended or resumed. Null until proven.
- `unproven_since` (timestamp?): For a request not proven gone that no longer awaits an answer in agent-director's records: when its record stopped awaiting one (its relay hook's ack, its pane answer's or record-pane-answer's write, or the close of its spawn's requests; a request with no recorded settle instant: its recorded verdict). Null while it still awaits an answer, and once proven gone.

### Errors

- `ErrMissingRequestToken`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrRelayModeOff`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrAmbiguousRequest`
- `ErrInvalidDecision`
- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrStoreBusy`

## get-permission

Fetch a request by request_token. decision and decided_at are null while undecided; a decided request can remain open until acknowledged. Read delivery for the outcome.

### Parameters

- `request_token` (string, required): UUIDv4 token identifying the permission_requests row to fetch.

### Result

- `request_token` (string): UUIDv4 token the row is keyed under (echoed back).
- `request_id` (int): Autoincrement primary key of the permission_requests row.
- `tool_name` (string): The agent's tool that triggered the permission request (e.g. "Bash", "Write").
- `tool_input` (string): Raw JSON string of the tool's input, NOT a nested JSON object; consumers parse it themselves.
- `requested_at` (timestamp): RFC3339 timestamp when the request was recorded.
- `decision` (string?): "allow" or "deny" once a verdict is recorded; null while undecided, and for a record-pane-answer claiming unknown. A recorded verdict is not the outcome: read delivery and pane_answer.
- `decision_reason` (string?): Canonical decision-reason string: for deny rows operator / timeout / find_missing / ended (find_missing and ended: the request was still undecided when find-missing marked its spawn missing, or when its spawn ended or was resumed, and is closed); for a request closed at the pane, allow or deny, pane (a pane answer through send-keys), pane_outside (record-pane-answer) or tool_ran (its tool ran); null while undecided and for allow rows decided by decide.
- `decided_at` (timestamp?): RFC3339 timestamp when the verdict was written; null while undecided.
- `delivery` (string): delivered: the relay hook acknowledged a verdict. not_confirmed: no ack yet and the hook may still run; it ends by confirm_by. fallen_back: no ack, and the hook is gone (or cannot be checked and confirm_by has passed): no answer from the relay reached the agent. While pane_answer is none or intent the request is open and only an answer at the pane, or record-pane-answer, closes it; with sent, outside or tool_ran it is closed. Derived on every read; a request with no recorded settle instant falls back by its relay window plus 2 s.
- `confirm_by` (timestamp): RFC3339 time by which not_confirmed ends: the relay hook's kill instant plus 2 s, by when its hook has acked (delivered) or is gone (fallen_back). With no recorded settle instant: requested_at plus the relay window plus 2 s.
- `hook_alive` (bool?): Whether the request's relay hook process runs, checked in the reader's pid namespace by its pid and start time: true; false (no such process, another start time, or a zombie); null when it cannot be checked (another or unreadable pid namespace, unreadable /proc, or no recorded hook identity).
- `hook_gone_at` (timestamp?): When a reader first found the request fallen back; null until then. A reading verb (get, list, get-permission) records it only if the store's write lock is free at that moment, never waiting.
- `attempted_decision` (string?): The verdict a decide refused as fallen back (ErrRelayFallenBack) tried to record, the latest one; null when none. Stored and shown, never acted on.
- `attempted_at` (timestamp?): When that refused decide ran; null when none.
- `tool_use_id` (string?): The permission request's tool_use_id from the agent's hook input; null when none was given.
- `pane_answer` (string): How the request was answered at the pane. none: no pane answer recorded through agent-director (something outside it, such as a person at tmux, may still have answered it). intent: a pane answer through send-keys was started and whether its key was typed is unknown. sent: its key was sent (decision_reason pane). outside: a caller recorded it answered outside agent-director (record-pane-answer, decision_reason pane_outside). tool_ran: the agent reported its tool ran (decision allow, decision_reason tool_ran). A request with sent, outside or tool_ran is closed and stays delivery fallen_back.
- `pane_as` (string?): The verdict a pane answer claims: allow, deny, or unknown (an outside record that did not see the answer); null when none was recorded. The caller's claim, stored and never checked.
- `proven_gone_at` (timestamp?): When the agent proved the request's permission dialog gone; null until then. agent-director's own records (delivered, a pane answer, record-pane-answer) are not proof. While it is null, plain send-keys to the live spawn without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused (ErrDialogMaybeOpen).
- `proven_gone_how` (string?): How it was proven gone. tool_ran: a Claude PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure carried its tool_use_id (never on a Codex row). turn_end: the turn of the agent that asked ended after it was written; the main agent's Stop or idle-prompt Notification, or a Codex main agent's Interrupt (Esc), proves a request with no agent_id (including a main-agent request). agent_gone: its spawn was marked missing, ended or resumed. Null until proven.
- `unproven_since` (timestamp?): For a request not proven gone that no longer awaits an answer in agent-director's records: when its record stopped awaiting one (its relay hook's ack, its pane answer's or record-pane-answer's write, or the close of its spawn's requests; a request with no recorded settle instant: its recorded verdict). Null while it still awaits an answer, and once proven gone.

### Errors

- `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`

## record-pane-answer

Close a fallen-back request answered outside agent-director; types nothing. Needs read-pane's pane_sha256; too soon: ErrClaimTooSoon.

### Parameters

- `request_token` (string, required): Token of the permission request answered outside agent-director (as get, get-permission or ErrRelayFallenBack's err_details name it). Accepted only while it has fallen back (its relay hook gone, no verdict acked, no pane answer completed) and no pane answer through send-keys on it is still being sent (else ErrPaneAnswerInProgress); acked or answered at the pane: ErrAlreadyDecided; closed with its spawn: ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest. Its relay hook must have been gone at least 2 s, from the request's hook_gone_at (written now when it has none), or from its confirm_by when earlier and the hook is judged by time (it cannot be checked, or the request has no recorded settle instant): the agent draws a dialog only after the hook ends, so a pane read sooner may not show it yet; else ErrClaimTooSoon with err_details.not_before (null only while the hook is seen running). Once recorded, plain send-keys is no longer refused with ErrRelayFallenBack on its account; without expect_pane_sha256 it is still refused with ErrDialogMaybeOpen until the agent proves the request gone (its proven_gone_at).
- `as` (string, required): How it was answered, as the caller claims: allow, deny, or unknown. Pass unknown unless the answer was seen. Recorded as pane_as, and as decision (null for unknown) with decision_reason pane_outside; never checked.
- `expect_pane_sha256` (string, required): Required. The pane_sha256 read-pane returned for the pane the caller looked at (64 hex digits). Before acting, the agent's pane is captured with the same n_lines, ANSI stripped as read-pane gives it by default, and its SHA-256 compared byte for byte; a difference is ErrPaneChanged, nothing done, and the error does not carry the new hash: read the pane again. It means a person or LLM judged this exact screen: never pass it from an automatic flow.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): The n_lines of the read-pane expect_pane_sha256 came from. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted.

### Result

- `request_token` (string): The request's token (echoed back).
- `pane_answer` (string): Always outside: the request is closed as answered outside agent-director.
- `pane_as` (string): The claim recorded.
- `decision` (string?): The claim when allow or deny; null for unknown.
- `decision_reason` (string): Always pane_outside.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrClaimTooSoon`
- `ErrPaneAnswerInProgress`
- `ErrPaneChanged`
- `ErrStoreBusy`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## resume

Relaunch a finished (ended/missing) row's latest agent session. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). Same id and JSONL transcript, fresh tmux session. Before its launch, resume runs spawn's best-effort pre-trust for the row's cwd, unless the row's latest spawn turned it off with no_pre_trust; a pre-trust failure never fails the resume. Returns the instance_id and pre_trust (ok, skipped or failed). Resume moves the row to pending, keeping its session id and history; parent_id becomes the caller's AGENT_DIRECTOR_INSTANCE_ID. The row stays pending until the agent reports in, then waiting. If the launch fails without timing out (ErrTmuxNotAvailable is ENVIRONMENT and ErrTmuxSessionCreate a LAUNCH FAILURE), resume restores the row's prior ended or missing state; if it cannot, the error says so. Creating the session is bounded by the create timeout; on a timeout resume returns ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE, transient): the session may have been created and the row stays pending; do not retry until get shows the row ended or missing. A refusal before the move writes nothing; resume can be re-issued. A session in the way (holding the name, left over, or this row's own) is never touched: ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT, until a human looks; see docs/operator-actions.md), or ErrTmuxUnresponsive while it appears to still be stopping or starting. A name held at the create is refused likewise, after the restore. A pending row (a launch in progress, a resumed one included) is refused with ErrSpawnNotResumable. A row whose instance id contains a control character (its session cannot be labelled) or whose recorded name is unusable (see kill) is refused with ErrInternal and no tmux call. If the store cannot record the launch, resume returns ErrInternal and launches nothing.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the finished (ended or missing) row to resume. Replay removes parsed session selectors, Claude print mode and cloud controls orphaned by selector removal without changing stored agent_args. Claude inputs missing a recognized required value get literal filtering only; otherwise arguments and option-owned values retain parsed meaning. Claude prompts move behind surviving options and --, and altered short clusters are re-encoded, only when needed to preserve that meaning; otherwise order and spelling survive.

### Result

- `instance_id` (string): The same id passed in (resume keeps the instance id).
- `pre_trust` (string): What the launch's folder-trust pre-trust did. ok = the folder trust took effect (claude: the entry was written to .claude.json; codex: the launch carries the folder trust and the hook-trust bypass); skipped = pre-trust was off for this launch because the row's latest spawn turned it off with no_pre_trust, so nothing was attempted; failed = pre-trust was attempted and the entry was not written (for a claude agent, the .claude.json file is missing, or could not be read, parsed or written, or the row's extra_env sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a path that is not absolute; for a codex agent, the row's extra_env sets CODEX_HOME to a path that is not absolute, and the launch carries neither the folder trust nor the hook-trust bypass); the launch still proceeds and the agent may stop at its folder-trust prompt (Claude Code's or Codex's).

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotResumable`
- `ErrNoSessionId`
- `ErrReservedEnvKey`
- `ErrJsonlMissing`
- `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSessionCreate`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## find-missing

Reconcile live rows with their agents. A row's liveness comes only from its agent process, checked by its recorded start time; no process environment is read; no child process or copy of the row's id keeps it alive. A dead agent process marks the row `missing` (a Codex row with an end report: `ended`, not in ids) whatever tmux shows, with no tmux call. Only a row whose process cannot be checked or was never recorded is looked up in tmux, once per socket, on its recorded socket (else the caller's): its own labelled session leaves it unverified (a row with no recorded pane is judged by the pane carrying its launch token, marked if none does), as does an unusable tmux answer; no session of its current launch marks it `missing` whatever holds its name. A session holding the name is never touched (see docs/operator-actions.md). tmux problems never fail the sweep. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. Run it as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents: a run as another user, as root or against another tmux server can mark live rows `missing`. See kill for what a wrong server leads to. Agents never run expire (operator-scheduled finished-row cleanup). ErrProbeUnsupported is no longer returned. A pending row (a spawn's, reuse's or resume's launch) is not judged inside the pending grace period (pending_grace_seconds, 60 s by default), measured from its launch start, not its started_at, or while its launch runs: it is in neither list; one with no readable launch start is judged at once. Past its grace, a pending row whose agent runs but no hook reported gets liveness_note unreported: read-pane, and only having looked, send-keys with allow_pending. To end a live row (pending included) and relaunch its id, follow the live-row sequence in kill's description.

### Parameters

_None._

### Result

- `count` (int): Number of rows this sweep marked `missing` (the length of ids); a Codex row it moved to `ended` is not counted. Zero is a legitimate happy-path result when nothing needed marking.
- `ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of rows this sweep marked `missing`, on process or tmux evidence: rows whose agent process (the SessionStart one or the recorded pane's) is dead, and rows whose process could not be checked and tmux found no session or pane of their current launch; a pending row only past the pending grace period, and never while the spawn, reuse or resume that began its launch still runs. A row whose guarded write found it changed or gone, or failed, is in neither list, and so is a Codex row the sweep moved to `ended` (its agent process gone and an end report held) and a pending row the sweep notes unreported (its agent alive) or finds already noted so. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. Never null; [] when none.
- `unverified` (int): Number of live rows this sweep left unverified (the length of unverified_ids).
- `unverified_ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of live rows this sweep left unverified with a liveness note, whether it wrote the note or found it already current: rows whose agent process could not be checked and which tmux did not mark, for example because their own session is present, tmux could not tell or was unavailable, or tmux was not called, or their recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, a control character, or a character tmux stores differently: no tmux call, and a liveness note of its own; removing such a row is a human's decision, see docs/operator-actions.md). Never a pending row inside the pending grace period or while its launch runs. A row whose guarded write found it changed or gone, or failed, a row whose note was cleared, and a pending row noted unreported (its agent alive, no hook reported since its launch; find it by liveness_note in get or list) are in neither list. Never null; [] when none.

### Errors

- `ErrProbeUnsupported`

## expire

Delete finished rows (ended/missing) whose ended_at is older than the retention window (defaults.expire_retention_days; older_than overrides). It reads tmux to decide, deleting a row only if its agent's recorded process is not seen running and tmux shows no session of the agent. It never kills a session or touches transcripts. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). Finished rows are removed by an operator-scheduled expire at the default retention, run as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents; it keeps and reports rows whose session runs or cannot be checked. Agents never run it, least of all with a zero window. A run as another user, as root or against another tmux server can wrongly delete rows.

### Parameters

- `older_than` (duration, optional): Duration override (e.g. `7d`, `2h`). When omitted, defaults.expire_retention_days from config applies.

### Result

- `count` (int): Number of rows deleted (the length of ids): rows deleted after tmux showed no session of the agent (Gone) and its recorded process was not seen running. Zero is a legitimate result when no row was deleted.
- `ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of the rows deleted after tmux showed no session of the agent (Gone) and its recorded process was not seen running, each only while the row was unchanged since expire examined it. Never null; [] when none.
- `kept` (int): Number of selected rows kept rather than deleted (the length of kept_ids), for example because the agent's process or a session of the agent (its own, or a leftover of an earlier launch) may still run, tmux could not be checked or answered from a different server, the run's tmux time budget (sweep_budget_seconds) was spent, the row changed after it was examined, or its recorded tmux session name cannot be used (kept on every run, before any other check, with no tmux call).
- `kept_ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of the selected rows kept rather than deleted, each reported with its reason in the trail (ad.expire.kept). A row whose recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, a control character, or a character tmux stores differently) is kept on every run, before any other check, with no tmux call and a reason of its own; removing it is a human's decision (see docs/operator-actions.md). tmux problems and a failed delete of one row never fail the run: the row is kept. A failed read of the selected rows fails the run. A row another caller removed first is in neither list. Never null; [] when none.

### Errors

_None._

## make-template

Save a spawn preset as ~/.config/agent-director/templates/NAME.toml. Per-invocation params (template, instance_id, tmux_session_name, reuse_finished) are refused.

### Parameters

- `name` (string, required): Template name. Must be filename-safe (no path separators, no leading dot, no `..`).
- `cwd` (string, optional): Bake a default cwd into the template. Per-call cwd overrides.
- `agent` (string, optional): Bake the template's agent: claude (Claude Code) or codex (Codex), case-sensitive; empty or absent means none, and no agent key is stored. Another value is refused with ErrTemplateMalformed. A non-empty agent_args needs an agent (ErrTemplateAgentMissing): the arguments belong to it. A codex template with any allow, deny or ask entry is refused with ErrPermissionsUnsupported. A spawn that names no agent takes the template's.
- `relay_mode` (string, optional): Bake a default relay_mode (on/off). Per-call relay_mode (--relay-mode on the CLI) overrides.
- `agent_args` ([]string, optional): Bake default agent argv. Per-call agent_args (on the CLI, spawn's arguments after --) REPLACES the template's array wholesale (not concat).
- `extra_env` (map[string]string, optional): Bake env-var entries. Per-call extra_env (--extra-env on the CLI) merges by key; per-call wins on collision. A key spawn would refuse is refused here by the same check with ErrReservedEnvKey, never rewritten, and no file is written: the reserved names AGENT_DIRECTOR_* and HOME with any value (set an absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code) or CODEX_HOME (Codex) to give the agent its own config), and a key that is not a valid env-var name (empty, or containing '=' or a NUL byte; the message says which).
- `label` ([]string, optional): Bake label k=v entries. Per-call label merges by key; per-call wins on collision.
- `allow` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.allow entries. Per-call allow CONCATENATES (does not replace).
- `deny` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.deny entries. Per-call deny CONCATENATES.
- `ask` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.ask entries. Per-call ask CONCATENATES.
- `overwrite` (bool, optional): Replace any existing template at this name atomically. Default false refuses an existing template.

### Result

- `path` (string): Absolute path of the written template file.

### Errors

- `ErrTemplateNameUnsafe`
- `ErrTemplateExists`
- `ErrTemplateMalformed`
- `ErrTemplateAgentMissing`
- `ErrPermissionsUnsupported`
- `ErrReservedEnvKey`

## list

Enumerate rows. All filters AND together. Order is unspecified; callers sort.

### Parameters

- `state` ([]string, optional): Filter by state. Multiple values OR together. Comma-separated on CLI; JSON array via MCP. With [state] settle_ms set it matches the settled state each row's state shows, before limit applies.
- `label` ([]string, optional): Filter by label k=v. Repeatable on CLI; each entry must contain a literal `=`. Multiple entries AND together.
- `parent` (string, optional): Filter by parent_id exact match.
- `cwd` (string, optional): Filter by canonicalized cwd exact match.
- `tmux_session_name` (string, optional): Filter by tmux session name exact match. Returns any live or ended row whose tmux_session_name equals the value byte-for-byte; correlation across re-uses, not uniqueness enforcement. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling, so list is not filtered by session name.
- `limit` (int, optional): Cap result count. 0 / omitted means no cap. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).

### Result

- `spawns` ([]Spawn): Matching rows. Empty array when none match (never null). Each row carries agent (string: claude or codex, the agent it runs) and liveness_unverified_since (timestamp?, the time a sweep first noted the row, kept while the note changes) and liveness_note (string?, the latest sweep's reason token, overwritten when the reason changes; or unreported on a pending row whose agent is alive but has not reported through any hook since its launch, kept by a sweep that finds the agent alive and cleared by the agent's next hook: read-pane, and only having looked, send-keys with allow_pending (--allow-pending on the CLI)), both omitted while NULL and cleared together when a sweep finds the agent process alive (except on a pending row noted unreported or provenance_conflict), and launch_started_at (timestamp?), the start of the launch in progress (RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision), omitted unless the row is pending. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms. Each row's state takes the same values as status, with the same meaning of pending: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) in progress whose agent has not reported in yet; a resumed pending row keeps its session id and history. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. With [state] settle_ms set in config.toml (whole milliseconds from 0 to 60000, 0 or unset is off; a value outside that range is refused, never capped), state is the settled state: a state a hook wrote shows only once it has held that long, and the last settled state shows meanwhile, so a change that reverts sooner never shows; ended, missing and a state a command wrote (spawn, resume, find-missing) show at once. Nothing marks a state as late, and the setting covers every caller on the host. A turn shorter than settle_ms never shows (a waiting agent that replies sooner reads waiting throughout), so keep it at 1000 to 2000. The row's other fields, and the verbs that act on it (send-keys, decide, pause, resume, kill, find-missing, expire, spawn), follow its live state, which can be newer: a refusal can name a state status does not show yet. Each row also carries permission_requests, as get's: Open permission requests: those that still await an answer (not acked by their relay hook and not answered at the pane, decided or not; a request with no recorded settle instant while undecided). Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Populated only when the row's live state is check_permission; empty array for all other states (a row can read waiting, working or ask_user while a request is still open: follow a tracked request with get-permission). Requests are never delayed by [state] settle_ms, so with it set a row can also read any state (even ended or missing) with open requests listed, or check_permission with [], for up to settle_ms. Each element: request_id (int) — autoincrement row id; request_token (string) — UUIDv4 request token, pass to decide verb to target this row; tool_name (string) — the agent's tool that triggered the request; tool_input (string) — raw JSON string of the tool's input, NOT a nested object (consumers parse it themselves); requested_at (RFC3339 timestamp) — when the request was recorded; decision and decision_reason (string?) — the recorded verdict, not the outcome; and the delivery facts as get-permission returns them: delivery (delivered, not_confirmed or fallen_back), confirm_by (timestamp), hook_alive (bool?), hook_gone_at (timestamp?), attempted_decision (string?), attempted_at (timestamp?), tool_use_id (string?), pane_answer (none or intent on an open request), pane_as (string?), proven_gone_at (timestamp?), proven_gone_how (string?) and unproven_since (timestamp?). get and list never wait for the store's write lock.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrListInvalidLabel`

## list-subagents

Return an agent's subagent records and whether they are tracked.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn whose subagents to list.

### Result

- `tracked` (bool): Whether the row's launch registered subagent tracking: false for a row launched before subagent tracking existed, which has no records, and false for a row whose launch registers no subagent events; true for any other row.
- `subagents` ([]object): Every subagent record of the row's current life, across every launch of it. Empty array when it has none (never null). Ordered by first_started_at ascending (records with a null first_started_at last), then subagent_id. Each element has all of these keys, a field with no known value null: subagent_id (string) — the subagent's id, unique among the records shown for its row; instance_id (string) — the row's id; session_id (string?) — the session of the event that created the record, never changed after; subagent_type (string?) — its type; description (string?) — the short description the launching call gave it, never the prompt text; model (string?) — the model it runs; parent_type (string?) — what launched it: agent (the row's own agent, so parent_id is the row's instance_id) or subagent (another subagent, so parent_id is that subagent's subagent_id); parent_id (string?) — as parent_type says; tool_use_id (string?) — the id of the tool call that launched it; run_mode (string?) — background or foreground; first_started_at (timestamp?) — when it first started; started_at (timestamp?) — when its latest run started; stopped_at (timestamp?) — when it last stopped, null if it never has (kept when it runs again); lost_at (timestamp?) — when it was judged lost, null unless it was; state (string) — running (started, neither stopped nor judged lost), stopped (its agent reported it finished) or lost (judged gone without a stop report); close_reason (string?) — why it is no longer running, null exactly while state is running: stop_event (its agent reported it finished), absent_from_snapshot (a snapshot of the agent's running background tasks did not list it) or agent_gone (its agent ended, went missing or began a new launch). Each timestamp is RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision (trailing zeros dropped, no fraction on a whole second).

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

## pause

Shut down a waiting row: type `/exit`, wait pause.timeout_seconds for `ended`. Ended/missing: no-op success. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). Codex: once the agent is gone with an end report, ends the row (before the keys or in the wait). Held as plain send-keys; past ErrDialogMaybeOpen: answer any dialog, send-keys `/exit` with expect_pane_sha256; or kill. ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed: input lock/journal failure. tmux errors: ErrTmuxSendKeys (GONE: only it means the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to pause.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotPausable`
- `ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed`
- `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrDialogMaybeOpen`
- `ErrPauseTimeout`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSendKeys`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## serve

Start the long-lived MCP server: the CLI verbs except `hook`, `serve` and `trail-emit` as MCP tools, JSON-RPC on stdio.

### Parameters

- `stdio` (bool, required): Enter the stdio MCP loop.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

_None._

## version

Print the version stamp as JSON ({version, commit, config_dir}). CLI aliases: --version, -v.

### Parameters

_None._

### Result

- `version` (string): Human-readable version stamp from `git describe --tags --always --dirty` at build time. "dev" for unstamped builds.
- `commit` (string): Full git SHA the binary was built from. "unknown" for unstamped builds.
- `config_dir` (string): Directory the binary keeps agent-director's files in: "~/.config/agent-director", unexpanded, for every HOME.

### Errors

_None._

## trail-emit

Emit an ad.* trail event (sub-verb relay-attempt) without opening state.db.

### Parameters

- `sub_verb` (string, required): Sub-verb to invoke. Currently: relay-attempt.
- `token` (string, required): request_token. Required.
- `endpoint` (string, required): target_endpoint (URL or socket path). Required.
- `outcome` (string|int, required): 3-digit HTTP status code (100-599, emitted as integer) or named error class: connection_refused, timeout, dns_failure (emitted as string). Required.
- `bytes_sent` (int, optional): Bytes sent. Default 0. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `bytes_received` (int, optional): Bytes received. Default 0. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `instance_id` (string, required): instance_id. Required.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrTrailWrite`

## hook

Internal: run by each agent's hooks; only the row's own agent's hooks write (others: ad.hook.ignored). Exits 0 (fail-open).

### Parameters

- `stdin` (json, required): Agent hook payload (hook_event_name, transcript_path, tool_name, reason, ...).
- `agent` (string, optional): The agent whose hook this is. Absent: claude. Any other value is a hook failure (fail-open; a relayed PermissionRequest is denied).
- `timeout` (int, optional): The per-hook timeout, in seconds, spawn wrote for this hook in the agent's settings (the PermissionRequest entry: the relay window). The relay hook's kill instant is its start plus it; the hook never acks a verdict without 2 s left before it. Absent, unparseable or not positive: the loaded config's relay.timeout_seconds.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

_None._
